It was archived in 2019 and has no tagged software release or evidence in this review of current CFPB use or independent adoption, so it does not yet clear the maturity/notability gate for a standalone product.

public_source.note: The archived public repository contains the scrub.sh utility, Node dependencies, installation and usage instructions, and checklist material.

eligible_license.note: The exact root LICENSE contains the CC0 1.0 Universal dedication. The functional scrub script was added in commit c7b4ef1 on 2016-06-10; the CC0 license file is present from the initial project commit aa03ded on the same date.

product_identity: CFPB open-source release-preparation helper; shell/Node tooling to scrub internal GitHub Enterprise URLs before public release, not the separate checklist template itself

Repository archived 2019-02-02.

decision_reason: The source is a real Boston/Code for America civic web application with an eligible BSD-3-Clause grant and documented installation, launch, and Honolulu reuse. However, the official Boston page is a retrospective pilot/lessons-learned page (about 100 volunteers, limited use), not evidence of current operation; the repository's default-branch commits.atom shows the latest master commit was 2016-10-12, despite repository-level pushed_at reflecting activity on another branch. Hold until a current deployment/support signal is found or an editorial Archived exception is approved for its historical significance.

government_provenance.note: Boston.gov states the City created the tool in 2011 with Boston Fire, Emergency Management, and Code for America fellow Erik Michaels-Ober, and says the City launched it in January 2011.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Rails application, tests, and installation, setup, seed-data, usage, and deployment instructions; Boston.gov links directly to this repository.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE.md grants BSD-3-Clause rights. Its 2011 copyright and license history show the file was added on 2011-04-28, establishing 2011 as the first defensible public licensed-source year for the existing application.

primary_evidence.note: Boston.gov documents the historical January 2011 launch, about 100 volunteers, limited pilot use, and Honolulu's reuse, and links this repository. It does not establish continuing 2026 operation/support. The repository's default-branch commit feed ends 2016-10-12; a 2023 pushed_at timestamp reflects a non-default branch and is not substantive current-source evidence.

product_identity: Adopt-a-Hydrant — Rails web application that let residents claim Boston fire hydrants and commit to clearing them after snowstorms
agency: City of Boston Mayor's Office of New Urban Mechanics, with Boston Fire Department and Emergency Management; built with Code for America fellow Erik Michaels-Ober
geography: United States (Boston, Massachusetts; civic-software model reused by Honolulu)
status_note: Hold for current-use/source-parity decision. The official City page is still reachable but presents the app as an experiment with limited use and retrospective results; no current deployment/support was established. GitHub's master commits.atom ends 2016-10-12; repository-level pushed_at in 2023 is from another branch. Coordinator may consider Archived only if the historical significance merits the baseline exception.

decision_reason: The Department of Health/HSE launched the exact COVID Tracker Ireland mobile app and published its source; the public repository contains the React Native iOS/Android source, setup and run instructions, and an initial 2020 commit with the MIT license. Ireland's official service page documents nationwide use and shutdown in August 2023, and an official 2020 release documents code reuse by other public-health authorities and U.S. states. This qualifies as a clearly labeled Archived historical record: a nationally deployed COVID-response application with government-to-government source reuse.

government_provenance.note: The Department of Health states HSE and the Department led development with government and technical partners, and that the source code for Ireland's official app was published; the official service page identifies the app as an Irish Government/HSE service.

public_source.note: The assigned public archive contains iOS and Android React Native source and build/run instructions. Its first commit (44da0f7, 2020-06-27) is titled Initial commit and includes the published app source.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE grants MIT rights. GitHub's LICENSE file history records the MIT LICENSE in the 2020-06-27 initial commit (44da0f7) alongside the source, supporting 2020 as the first public licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The Department of Health documents that public-health authorities in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Northern Ireland, Scotland, Gibraltar, and Jersey launched apps based on the Irish source. The official service page states the Irish app closed completely at the start of August 2023.

product_identity: COVID Tracker Ireland — HSE/Department of Health mobile contact-tracing, symptom-tracking, and COVID information app; repository contains its iOS/Android client source
agency: Health Service Executive (HSE) and Department of Health, Ireland
geography: Ireland; source reused by other national/subnational public-health authorities
status_note: Archived: contact tracing ended and the app was switched off in August 2023; GitHub archive was set on 2026-03-09. Retain only as an unusually significant historical national public-health app with documented government-to-government source reuse. Do not imply the service remains operational.

decision_reason: NLR's official software page lists API Umbrella as an NLR-developed open-source product and links the repository now hosted by its National Laboratory of the Rockies organization. The current GSA api.data.gov page states that its production service is powered by API Umbrella and links this project. The assigned repo provides the active API management platform source, installation/development documentation, and an MIT grant. The first root license commit is 2012-09-03; default-branch functional maintenance continues in 2026.

government_provenance.note: NLR's official software catalog describes API Umbrella, identifies it as an NLR software offering, and links https://github.com/NREL/api-umbrella, which resolves to the assigned NatLabRockies repository after the lab's GitHub organization migration.

public_source.note: The repository publicly provides the platform source. The default branch has substantive 2026 commits (including PostgreSQL/dependency and installation updates); the API.data.gov production source link resolves to this repository.

eligible_license.note: The project root contains an MIT grant for API Umbrella code; bundled/third-party dependencies have their own licenses. GitHub history records the root license being added on 2012-09-03 (commit 50ae4bc), establishing 2012 as the first public licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The current official GSA api.data.gov service page says the production federal API-management service is powered by the open-source API Umbrella project and links its source. NLR also publishes API Umbrella as its own software product and supplies user/deployment documentation.

product_identity: API Umbrella — NLR API management platform for exposing and operating web-service APIs; includes proxy, admin UI, API key/access management, rate limiting, and analytics
agency: National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly National Renewable Energy Laboratory), U.S. Department of Energy; also deployed by GSA Technology Transformation Services for api.data.gov
geography: United States (federal; NLR and GSA deployments)
license: MIT for API Umbrella-authored project code; bundled third-party dependencies retain their respective licenses
status_note: Active. The default branch has substantive 2026 maintenance. NLR's official catalog directly identifies the product and source; api.data.gov's current GSA page documents the production deployment and links the same source. Repository-level pushed_at must not be used as a substitute for default-branch source history.

decision_reason: GeoQ is real NGA-developed MIT software with publicly available Django source, install/run instructions, and documented historical disaster-response coordination with NGA/FEMA. However, the default develop branch commit feed ends 2020-09-16 (over 6 years ago), and I found no current product-specific government deployment or support signal; GitHub's newer pushed_at reflects activity outside the default branch. Hold pending current-use/source-parity evidence or an explicit archived-history determination.

government_provenance.note: The White House OSTP report describes GeoQ as developed in coordination with NGA, the Presidential Innovation Fellows program, FEMA, and disaster analysts. The project README says NGA developed the software with MITRE and released it under MIT.

eligible_license.note: The project root contains an MIT grant. GitHub history shows the LICENSE was first created on 2014-06-23 (commit b2b38fb), establishing 2014 as the first public licensed-source year.

primary_evidence.note: The White House report establishes historical disaster-response purpose and government collaboration, but it is from 2014. No current product-specific deployment/support or independent current use was found, and no post-2020 default-branch code activity was found.

product_identity: GeoQ — Django geographic work-queue/tasking web application for collecting and coordinating geospatial observations across large areas
agency: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, developed with FEMA/Presidential Innovation Fellows and MITRE
status_note: Hold for current-source use/support or archival-history decision. The GitHub org page describes its account as NGA's official organizational account; README and White House report support origin and historical mission. Default branch develop last committed 2020-09-16; repository-level pushed_at/other-branch activity does not establish current product maintenance.

decision_reason: Madison is a real GPL-3.0 legislative-engagement application, but it was developed and operated by the nonprofit OpenGov Foundation. Historical use by lawmakers and governments is not evidence that government authored, commissioned, funded, or owned this source. The Foundation's own 2019 announcement says the hosted platform shut down; this lead is not eligible government software under the baseline.

government_provenance.note: The project owner OpenGov Foundation states it developed Madison for public servants and citizens and operated it as a nonprofit platform; the evidence found documents government use, not government authorship, commissioning, or funding of this source.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Laravel/PHP application source and project documentation.

eligible_license.note: GitHub identifies the root code grant as GNU GPL-3.0.

primary_evidence.note: The source owner says Madison was a nonprofit-developed service and announced its hosted platform shutdown for 2019-02-10. Government users are users of third-party software, not a government product relationship.

product_identity: Madison — OpenGov Foundation's legislative document feedback and public-engagement web platform
agency: No qualifying government creator, commissioner, or funder established; source owner/developer is the OpenGov Foundation nonprofit
geography: United States and other historical government-user jurisdictions
status_note: Reject for government-provenance scope, not for lack of software identity: the Foundation documents broad government use and historical significance, but the user requirement is government-created/commissioned/funded/stewarded software, not third-party services used by public officials.

The repository README explicitly describes it as customized Finda code, and its latest branch commit was 2021-08-11; the service evidence I found is historical (2015/2016), so current government support/use and whether this local fork merits a separate product entry remain unresolved.

public_source.note: The assigned public repository contains the local JavaScript/HTML app, Lexington treatment-resource data, test commands, and development instructions.

eligible_license.note: The repository's root license file is identified by GitHub as MIT. Its history predates the local fork, so this review treats MIT as the inherited Finda source grant and does not infer a standalone public-release year for the Lexington customization.

README identifies this repo as a customization of Code for Boston's Finda, so independent product boundary also needs coordinator judgment.

decision_reason: This is an official open-source release of CHVote v1's offline election-administration application plus the utility libraries it needs, not the complete online voting platform. The repository identifies the Geneva State Chancellery and Geneva IT Department as collaborators, publishes AGPL-3.0 code and detailed build/run guidance, and Geneva's 2017 announcement identifies this exact released component and records use of the larger CHVote platform by six cantons. The operational platform was discontinued in 2019 and this repository was archived in 2026; retain only as an historically significant, multi-canton election-software component, with the scope limitation explicit.

government_provenance.note: The repository README says CHVote resulted from collaboration between the Geneva State Chancellery and Geneva IT Department; Geneva's official 2017 release page confirms the canton published the source.

public_source.note: The public repository provides the offline administration application's source, utility libraries, documentation, and build/run steps.

eligible_license.note: The repository license and README release the components under GNU AGPL version 3.0, an OSI-approved license; this claim is scoped to the published offline application and included utilities, not undisclosed platform components.

primary_evidence.note: Geneva's official announcement says the previously published source was the component used to generate encryption keys and decrypt the ballot box, records substantial public review, and a separate Geneva release reports CHVote was used by six cantons. The repository supplies compiling/running guidance. Geneva later discontinued v1 operation in 2019; the historical importance is the publicly audited election component and multi-canton service, not current use.

product_identity: CHVote v1 offline administration application and required utility libraries; one security-critical released component, not the complete CHVote online voting system
agency: State Chancellery and General Directorate of Information Systems, Republic and Canton of Geneva
geography: Geneva, Switzerland; CHVote service used in six Swiss cantons in 2017
license: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)
status_note: Archived / historical. The source repo was archived on 2026-05-22. Geneva ended CHVote v1 operations in 2019. The only admitted identity is the released offline administration app plus required utilities; do not describe this repository as the full voting platform.
